#001

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00001
High Custom + axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A High - detected by both engines
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: a[href$="www.cisco.com"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a target="_blank" href="http://www.cisco.com">
                                            <div class="partner cisco"></div>
                                        </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

Custom scanner evidence

Link has no accessible name. Add meaningful link text, aria-label, or image alt text.

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" href="http://www.cisco.com" target="_blank">
<div class="partner cisco"></div>
</a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

#013

Heading hierarchy may be inconsistent

Medium Custom + axe Headings WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships Level A High - detected by both engines
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Unexpected heading-level jumps can make the relationship between sections harder to understand.

Location

DOM selector: a[href$="fass"] > .will-change-transform.lqd-fb-content-wrap[data-stacking-factor="0.5"] > .py-1\/5em.px-1\/5em.justify-end > .mb-1\/50em.mt-0 | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<h6 class="mt-0 mb-1/50em font-bold ">
                                        Faculty of Art And Social Sciences
                                    </h6>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Heading order invalid

Custom scanner evidence

Heading level jumps from H2 to H6.

axe description

Ensure the order of headings is semantically correct

Recommended change

Review the document outline and use heading levels according to the logical content hierarchy.

Manual review

Required: Yes

A heading-level jump is not automatically a WCAG failure. The full document hierarchy must be reviewed.

Why this matters

Location

DOM selector: .lqd-section-flow-item.items-center.flex:nth-child(2) > .talent.lqd-section-flow-item-inner > .py-20percent.flex-wrap.flex > .ld-fancy-heading.relative > .text-42.leading-0\/9em.mb-0\/75em | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<h2 class="ld-fh-element inline-block relative text-42 leading-0/9em mb-0/75em">
                                                    AIUB Crowned Champions of Inter-University Futsal Tournament 2026
                                                </h2>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element has insufficient color contrast of 1.23 (foreground color: #e6e6e6, background color: #fefeff, font size: 31.5pt (42px), font weight: normal). Expected contrast ratio of 3:1

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

View issue details and remediation

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

<div class="text-20">

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

color-contrast  •  UF-00244
Review axe — manual review Color contrast WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA Manual review required
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: .hover\:text-primary.text-gray-300[href$="fass"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a class="text-gray-300 hover:text-primary" href="/faculties/fass">
                                                    Faculty of Arts &amp; Social
                                                    Sciences
                                                </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element's background color could not be determined because it is overlapped by another element

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

Methodology note: Automated accessibility testing can identify many important problems, but it cannot establish complete WCAG conformance. Context-dependent and incomplete findings require human review. Context-aware recommendations are produced by deterministic rules using extracted local page context and should be verified before implementation.
